pr_title: Add support for Stretch product to Plugwise integration
pr_body:
## Proposed change
Add support for [Plugwise Stretch](https://www.plugwise.com/nl_NL/het-systeem) for switching devices (i.e. this makes using older circle/stealth plugs possible). Within restructuring for these plugs we also can close #38238. As per request link to our [Changelog](https://github.com/plugwise/Plugwise-Smile/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) for the version bump for the final modifications for Stretch support. Additionally some minor corrections (sorting CONSTs and better usage of CONSTs) and additional fixtures for the stretch platform (and config_flow accordingly).

## Type of change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New integration (thank you!)
- [x] New feature (which adds functionality to an existing integration)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information

- This PR fixes or closes issue: fixes #38238 #42725
- This PR is related to issue: #42684 
- Link to documentation pull request: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/14508

## Checklist

- [x] The code change is tested and works locally.
- [x] Local tests pass. **Your PR cannot be merged unless tests pass**
- [x] There is no commented out code in this PR.
- [x] I have followed the [development checklist][dev-checklist]
- [x] The code has been formatted using Black (`black --fast homeassistant tests`)
- [x] Tests have been added to verify that the new code works.

If user exposed functionality or configuration variables are added/changed:

If the code communicates with devices, web services, or third-party tools:

- [x] The [manifest file][manifest-docs] has all fields filled out correctly.  
      Updated and included derived files by running: `python3 -m script.hassfest`.
- [x] New or updated dependencies have been added to `requirements_all.txt`.  
      Updated by running `python3 -m script.gen_requirements_all`.
- [ ] Untested files have been added to `.coveragerc`.

To help with the load of incoming pull requests:

- [x] I have reviewed one other [open pull requests][prs] in this repository in the past week. (PR 39963)

issue_context.title: Plugwise P1 Smile reporting same energy consumption for peak and off_peak, not reporting production (interval)
issue_context.body: ## The integration Plugwise is reporting the same energy consumption for the peak and the off_peak entity/ Also the energy production off_peak int is reporting 0.0 where there should be some, according to my solaredge panels. ## Environment - Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.117.1 - Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): unknown - Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): Home Assistant OS - Integration causing this issue: Plugwise - Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/plugwise/ ## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml` ```yaml ``` ## Traceback/Error logs ```txt ``` ## Additional information My configuration.yaml is completely broken up in pieces, therefor my configuration.yaml is almost empty (I've followed the same structure like Frenck has.). However. this integration does not have anything in the configuration.yaml anyway. Explanation also given in attached screen shots.
comments:
Hey there @compatech, @bouwew, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`plugwise`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L330) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

I'm seeing some errors in the code, in sensor.py:
```
    "electricity_produced_off_peak_point": [
        "Current Consumed Power (off peak)",
        POWER_WATT,
        DEVICE_CLASS_POWER,
    ],
    "electricity_produced_peak_point": [
        "Current Consumed Power",
        POWER_WATT,
        DEVICE_CLASS_POWER,
    ],
    "electricity_produced_off_peak_cumulative": [
        "Cumulative Consumed Power (off peak)",
        ENERGY_KILO_WATT_HOUR,
        DEVICE_CLASS_POWER,
    ],
    "electricity_produced_peak_cumulative": [
        "Cumulative Consumed Power",
        ENERGY_KILO_WATT_HOUR,
        DEVICE_CLASS_POWER,
    ],
```
"Consumed" in the names should be "Produced".
Sorry about that.

We will provide a fix for this in the already existing PR https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/40108

Thanks, but that does not seem to relate to the issue that consumed_off_peak_point and consumed_peak_point display the same consumption at the same time (they can never have a value at the same time for point values).
I have checked today, during peak time on a workday and it seems to show the consumed_peak_point correctly, while consumed_off_peak_point is 0 at the moment.

My screenshots come from the weekend. During the weekend, there should only be a consumed_off_peak_point throughout the entire weekend. consumed_peak_point should only be displaying a number other than 0 during the peak hours on working days.

The numbers for produced_peak_point, product_off_peak_point, produced_peak_int and produced_off_peak_int all show 0 as a value. I guess this does have to do with the issue you found in the code, but please also check the int. numbers as well, as they show 0 like the point numbers.

If you are interested, you can test with plugwise-beta: https://github.com/plugwise/plugwise-beta

You can nowadays switch seamless between the Core plugwise component and the plugwise-beta custom_component: when you install the custom_component and don't remove the Plugwise Integration(s), after a restart the custom_component will automatically load/take over. When you uninstall the custom_component and don't remove the Plugwise Integration(s), after a restart the Core Plugwise component will automatically load.

Installed the beta custom component. Data at this point in time looks good (peak), but I need to review at different times as well as it's nighttime and therefor no production.
Will review at some different points in time (off_peak, peak with production, and then during the weekend, when there should only be off_peak). Will keep you posted.
Thanks! Appreciate your help in testing :)

Sure, no worries. I appreciate all the work done on the integration.

So far, so good with testing. During workdays the consumed and produced sensors for both off_peak and peak display the correct numbers and switch correctly to off_peak at 23.00h and to peak at 07.00h.
Now, I have to wait until the weekend to see if the issue in the weekend is fixed where I saw consumed_peak and consumed_off_peak display the same value at the same time, where it should only display the consumed_off_peak_point.
Will report back on Saturday.

Checked the consumed_peak_point and consumed_off_peak_point. Only the off_peak_point provides a value now, instead of both showing the same value. So that's all good.
The beta component appears to be working perfectly.
I guess that this issue can be closed then, when it's merged into master.

Thanks for reporting!

Yes, the issue will automatically be closed when the mentioned PR has been merged.
